protein: KPC-2, the Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase-2 class A beta-lactamase; variants are cumulative genotypes from directed evolution toward ceftazidime
readout: log2 MIC (ug/ml) for ceftazidime, the oxyimino-cephalosporin selected for
assay_method: Minimum inhibitory concentration by twofold broth dilution for Escherichia coli carrying the evolved blaKPC allele, after successive rounds of error-prone PCR mutagenesis and selection on increasing ceftazidime. Values are read from Supplementary Table 2, covering all 18 evolutionary lines.
remark: Mutation labels are derived from the nucleotide changes the source prints beside each amino-acid change, translated against the blaKPC-2 coding sequence of GenBank AY034847, because the paper's own residue numbering is not a constant offset from the sequence and is internally inconsistent, the single change c587a appearing as S196Y in line H5 and S197Y in line L3; 61 of the 62 printed nucleotide positions carry the stated wild-type base and every derived residue identity matches the paper's, giving 39 distinct substitutions against the 40 the abstract counts. Genotypes are cumulative points along evolutionary trajectories rather than single mutants, carrying up to six substitutions, since the source states that mutations observed in one round are retained in later rounds and prints only the new ones. The readout is the base-2 logarithm of the MIC because the assay is a twofold dilution series, so the raw values are spaced geometrically. Supplementary Table 2 and the Source Data file disagree on one cell, line S1 round 3, at 2048 and 1024 micrograms per millilitre respectively; this file follows Supplementary Table 2 throughout, that being the only source covering all 18 lines. Supplementary Table 2 is supplied as an image rather than as text, so it was read visually; the reading was checked against the cumulative non-synonymous mutation counts in the Source Data file, which agree for all 48 line and round combinations they share.

protein: TnpB, an RNA-guided DNA endonuclease of the IS200/IS605 transposon family; variants are single substitutions across the whole protein
readout: Normalized log2 enrichment in a selection for TnpB genome editing, the single-substitution scan across all 408 residues
assay_method: Ribonucleoprotein mutational scanning: a barcoded library of TnpB variants is expressed in Escherichia coli alongside its reRNA guide, and cells in which the ribonucleoprotein cleaves its genomic target are depleted, so a variant's change in abundance reports editing activity. Long-read sequencing associates barcodes with genotypes and short-read sequencing counts them before and after selection; the score is the median normalized log2 enrichment over two replicates.
remark: The wild-type sequence is the 408-residue TnpB open reading frame read out of the reference plasmid the deposit ships, data/protein/protein_ref_plasmid.fa; it is corroborated by the scan itself, whose OriginalAA column is consistent at every one of the 406 positions it covers and reproduces residues 2 to 407 of that reading frame exactly, position 1 being the initiator methionine the library does not mutate and position 408 lying past the scan. 382 rows are dropped whose substitution is coded X, the library's nonsense variant at each position, a truncation having no substitution form in this format, and one further row labelled dead is dropped, being a catalytically inactivated control construct rather than a genotype. The readout is the source's own replicate-averaged normalized log2 enrichment and is used unchanged; the wild type is 0 by that normalization rather than by measurement. Not extracted from this paper: the reRNA library enrichment sheet of the same workbook, whose variants are changes to the guide RNA rather than substitutions in a protein and cannot be written against a protein sequence, and the plant and human-cell editing efficiencies, which are reported for a handful of variants only. The article PDF is not redistributed in papers/: the paper is hybrid open access with a publisher landing page and no PMC deposit, so these datasets are built from the authors' GitHub deposit SavageLab/tnpb_dms, whose README names this paper and its preprint.
